title: Gamescom 2026: Everything You Need to Know About the Opening
subtitle: Geoff Keighley Announces Eight Major Titles for the Opening Night Live
excerpt: Gamescom 2026 kicks off with the Opening Night Live on August 25, unveiling trailers and gameplay for titles like The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past and Final Fantasy.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The interest in Gamescom 2026 surged after the reveal of the titles to be showcased at the official opening, the Opening Night Live. The announcement, made by Geoff Keighley, brought eight heavyweight games, generating high anticipation among players and industry professionals.

Opening Night Live and the Broadcast Schedule

The opening event takes place on August 25, 2026, at 11 a.m. PT / 2 p.m. ET, and will be streamed live on Gamescom’s official YouTube channel. In some regions, the broadcast starts on the 26th due to time zone differences.

The Eight Confirmed Games

Among the confirmed titles are The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, a DLC that expands the RPG’s story, and Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which brings new content to Square Enix’s classic. While the exact content of each presentation is still unknown, most games are expected to receive a new trailer or gameplay footage.

Gamescom as the Main Showcase Post‑E3

With E3’s decline, Gamescom has solidified itself as the largest industry gathering, attracting all major publishers—Sony, Microsoft, Nintendo, EA, Activision—and maintaining a strong presence of PC companies like Riot and Blizzard. The event focuses on concrete demonstrations and playable code, especially for releases slated for the coming months.

Importance for the Brazilian Market

For Brazilian audiences, Gamescom offers the opportunity to see first‑hand the news that will arrive on consoles and PC, as well as access content that is typically revealed at international events.

How to Follow

Interested viewers can watch the live broadcast on Gamescom’s official YouTube channel starting at 11 a.m. PT / 2 p.m. ET on August 25. The full schedule, including regional times, is available on the convention’s website.

Information from VICE, Polygon.com.
